body:
> I would fully expect all physics callbacks to stop entirely once the program begins to quit

To a common misconception these signals are NOT physics callbacks.

They are just Area2D Node internal bookkeeping lists of overlaps getting updated. Some entries in that bookkeeping list may get updated after a real physics server sync but many are also just caused by signal-spaghettification with other Node objects and them changing tree and shape status.

So this here is a normal Node "leave" routine, to be more specific the Area2D node cleaning up its internal bookkeeping list of overlaps and emitting the related signals. Has nothing to do with the actual physics. If the entire SceneTree is tearing down all its Nodes follow their normal exit routine that just happens in whatever node order.

A signal can emit at any time, it is not bound to a Node or a Node being in a SceneTree. That some Nodes may not emit their signals while not inside the SceneTree is their own custom code but not a default behavior of signals so you can not expect that.

The example is using unsafe code in a signal callback that needs to be fixed. E.g. by doing a sanity check on objects before they are used. In the example any situation the node would be connected manual to the PhysicsServer callback but still outside the tree the script would also crash. Writing safe code so it does not crash on null objects is not a responsibility the engine can take away from users.

Would this be a documentation issue then? This distinction in behavior doesn't seem to be very clear (in fact, the "Consider using signals instead" line at the end of the documentation for the overlap list access functions makes it sound like the signals are more directly integrated into the physics callbacks rather than using the area's overlap list.)  That Area2D emits body_exited upon being removed (regardless of said removal being due to a quit or not) also seems unintuitive to me.

Also, I'd note that in the vast majority of cases where a node is outside the scene tree, it's because the node was removed from or created outside the tree explicitly by the programmer. There is no reason in normal operation to ever believe that a node has unpredictably left the scene tree, hence a sanity check on get_tree() not being intuitively necessary. The tree getting cleaned up during quit is very much a special case in this sense.

> Would this be a documentation issue then?

I have no good answer to that. I leave it to the documentation guys to decide. It is a delicate problem to solve to not only to find the right place where to add something to documentation but also find the right balance between too much or too little information.


As a general hint for safe dealing with signal callbacks that have external dependencies they should all be treated as if it is a static function. In the example turning the callback function into static would have immediately thrown and error on `get_tree()` revealing that that function is complete unsafe to be used in a signal context without a null check. The tree object is neither a static object or a singleton, so the engine can make zero guarantees that that object always exists in context of a signal callback.

Fair enough. I am definitely struggling to see a convenient place in the documentation to elaborate on this topic, but it does seem like important info to be documented somewhere, especially given I'm apparently not the first to get confused by how Area2D handles these things.
